Qabala, also known as Qabalah or Kabbalah, is a Jewish mystical tradition that is based on the idea that the universe is a manifestation of God and that by understanding the nature of God and the universe, one can achieve spiritual enlightenment and connection to the divine. The word "qabala" comes from the Hebrew word "qabalah," which means "receiving" or "reception."

Qabalistic teachings often involve the use of symbolism and mystical practices, such as meditation and visualization, to gain insights into the nature of the universe and to connect with the divine. Qabalistic practices also often involve the use of rituals, such as the creation of sacred spaces and the use of special tools, such as the sefirot, which are a set of ten divine attributes that represent different aspects of God's nature.

One of the central concepts in Qabala is the idea of the sefirot, which are ten attributes that are believed to represent the divine nature of God. These attributes include wisdom, understanding, mercy, compassion, strength, beauty, majesty, victory, foundation, and glory. By understanding and embodying these attributes, it is believed that one can gain greater insight into the nature of God and the universe and can achieve spiritual enlightenment.

Overall, Qabala is a complex and multifaceted tradition that has had a significant influence on Jewish spirituality and culture.
